messages:
alex: Opening thread  we need to finalize connector failover semantics + bootstrap for VPC-isolated installs. Draft idea attached below.
maya: want the failure modes spelled out. Is failover symmetric (controlplane->connector) or only connector->relay?
alex: connector->relay only for now. Controlplane will never initiate a data-plane swap unless operator triggers it.
sam: reasoning? If controlplane flips to relay it could break customer routing expectations. Also harder to explain in support.
irene: agree. But controlplane should be able to insist on relay if we detect policy violations or cert issues. That's an operator action (with audit).
dave: ops point  how do we detect 'connector unhealthy'? Is it just control channel heartbeat or active egress probes?
alex: heartbeat+active probe. Heartbeat window = 45s missed pings -> degraded. If active probe (HTTP GET to /health via local SNAT) fails 3/3 we promote relay.
maya: add hysteresis: only switch to relay after X consecutive windows and remain on relay for Y before retry (to avoid thrash).
sam: propose config: failover: {consecutive_windows:2, min_relay_duration:120s, retry_backoff: 30s}.
irene: certificate bootstrap: connectors create a CSR signed by local machine identity, send over the control channel. Controlplane CA returns short-lived mTLS cert. For airgapped, we support pre-signed cert bundle and a one-shot bootstrap token.
zoe: networking nit: path MTU. Many customers have smaller MTUs; connectors should do MSS clamping for proxied flows and advertise conservative MTU in health metadata.
dave: good catch. Add a smoke test for PMTU pitfalls (repro: client -> big response -> fragmentation stall).
ops-bot: task created OPS-1211: PMTU smoke + connector failover test
alex: sample contract (sketch): ```yaml
connector_api_version: v1
auth:
  method: signed_csr
  bootstrap_token_ttl: 1h
health:
  heartbeat_interval: 15s
  heartbeat_miss_threshold: 3
failover:
  consecutive_windows: 2
  min_relay_duration_s: 120
  retry_backoff_s: 30
observability:
  metric_labels: [path, region, connector_id, customer_snat_ip]
```
maya: metrics: add egress_bytes_by_path and token_exchange_latency. Also tag traces with failover_reason.
sam: security question: do we allow connector to rewrite Host header for internal service probing? I'd prefer explicit opt-in.
irene: must be opt-in and logged. Default = SNI passthrough; termination only if customer sets termination: true in onboarding.
\odave?: (typo) -- remove.
dave: billing question: ephemeral NAT allocations (per-customer ElasticIP or pooled ephemeral NAT) vs relay egress charges. Need simple pricing note in RFC.
alex: billing note: hybrid default means relay billed until connector used for production traffic; connector-only customers will incur NAT pool charges by region. We'll have a per-hour NAT reservation + per-GB egress offset.
\m aya?: (typo)
maya: add rollout plan: new customers default hybrid, 2-week internal opt-in window, then gradual ramp with health checks and SLO watch. Invite: network checklist + runbook.
sam: chaos run: disrupt control channel for 5m in staging and measure fallback success rate and request error spikes. Schedule after RFC.
irene: audit requirements: every forced-relay action must create an audit event with operator id, reason, and automated rollback window.
dave: owners: RFC (alex), cert spec & airgap flow (irene), metrics/traces (maya), chaos + smoke tests (sam/dave), billing blurb (finance-eng: zoe).
ops-bot: deploy-notice: connector-agent v2.4-rc pushed to staging (sha: def456)
zoe: small UX ask: console should show 'current egress path' and last failover time + cause. Helps support handoffs.
alex: will include UX wire in RFC appendix. I'll write full RFC and include sample configs, test plan, and migration checklist. Target: EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
